title: Positioning the reader

draft.title: Positioning the reader
card: Positioning means leading readers to feel a certain way about a character, event or issue. Writers and creators do this through the choices they make.
words carry feelings beyond their meaning. "Strolled" feels relaxed, but "slunk" feels sneaky, even though both describe walking.
what a writer includes or leaves out shapes our view. A character shown helping a stranger and sharing lunch seems kind.
pictures, or word pictures, can guide feelings too. A character shown small and alone in a huge dark room makes us feel sorry for them.
draft.remember: Writers choose words, details and images on purpose to steer how readers feel.

a.q: A writer says a new student "crept" into class, "clutching" her bag and staring at the floor. How is the reader positioned?
opts: To feel sympathy for the student
To feel angry at the student
To feel amused by the student
To feel jealous of the student
a.why: Words such as crept and clutching, along with staring at the floor, suggest she is nervous and shy. This leads readers to feel sympathy. Anger does not fit, because nothing she does harms anyone.
a.clue: Think about what crept and clutching suggest about her feelings.

b.q: Two reports describe the same footy coach. Report A says he "barked" orders and "stormed" off. Report B says he "called" orders and "walked" off. What is the main difference in how they position the reader?
opts: A leads readers to dislike him, B is more neutral
A leads readers to admire him, B is more neutral
A gives more facts about the match than B does
A and B lead readers to feel the same way about him
b.why: Barked and stormed carry feelings of anger and aggression, so Report A leads readers to view him badly. Called and walked are plain words. Both reports describe the same actions, so they do not differ in facts, only in word choice.
b.clue: Compare the feelings carried by the verbs, not the actions.

a.best: To feel sympathy for the student

b.best: A leads readers to dislike him, B is more neutral
